CPI for July

The consumer price index (CPI) increased 0.1% in July, compared with a fall of 0.4% in June,  according to the latest report from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. The year-over-year increase was 3.4%, down from 3.5% in June. The core CPI, excluding food and energy, was up 2.5% from a year ago, compared to 2.6% for the year ending in June.

results.content: Over the past six months, the US consumer has avoided a meaningful collapse, but broad strength remains elusive. Upper-income households ($100K+) are experiencing improvements in their outlook and spending behaviors, while lower- ($0–50K) and middle-income ($50K–100K) households continue to report signs of pressure. The result is an uneven experience across the income spectrum, with demand support becoming more concentrated at the upper end.
